results.title: Review — Π-Model, Temporal Ensembling: Temporal Ensembling for Semi-Supervised Learning | by Sik-Ho Tsang | Medium
results.content:
Title: Review — Π-Model, Temporal Ensembling: Temporal Ensembling for Semi-Supervised Learning | by Sik-Ho Tsang | Medium
# Review — Π-Model, Temporal Ensembling: Temporal Ensembling for Semi-Supervised Learning. > **Temporal Ensembling for Semi-Supervised Learning**. > **Π-Model, Temporal Ensembling**, by NVIDIA. > Semi-Supervised Learning, Image Classification. * During training, the network **evaluates each training input *xi* twice**, resulting in **prediction vectors *zi* and ~*zi***. 2. The **second** component, evaluated for **all inputs**, penalizes different predictions for the **same training input *xi***by taking the **mean square difference between the prediction vectors *zi* and ~*zi***. * Because of Dropout regularization, as well as Gaussian noise and augmentations, **there is difference between the prediction vectors *zi* and ~*zi* given the same original input *xi*.** However, the labels should be the same since they are coming from the same original input *xi*. * **The main difference to the Π-model** is that the network and augmentations are evaluated **only once per input** per epoch. * Because of Dropout regularization and stochastic augmentation, ***Z*** thus contains **a weighted average of the outputs of an ensemble of networks *f* from previous training epochs, with recent epochs having larger weight than distant epochs.**. * The benefits of temporal ensembling compared to Π-model are twofold:. 1. First, **the training is faster** because the network is evaluated only once per input on each epoch. 2. Second, the training targets ~*z* can be expected to be **less noisy than with Π-model.**. * **Π-model** obtains **16.55% error rate** on CIFAR-10. * **When augmentations were enabled, temporal ensembling further reduced the error rate to 5.12%.** In this test the difference between Π-model and temporal ensembling was quite significant at 1.5 percentage points. * **With 10000 labeled images, Π-model obtains error rates of 43.43% and 38.65% without and with augmentation, respectively.** These correspond to 7.8 and 5.9 percentage point improvements compared to supervised learning with labeled inputs only. * Unlabeled extra images improved the error rate by 2.7 percentage points (from 26.30% to 23.63%). results.title: What is Ensembling in Machine Learning? - California Learning Resource Network
results.content:
Title: What is Ensembling in Machine Learning? - California Learning Resource Network
Ensembling, in the context of machine learning, refers to the technique of combining multiple individual models to produce a superior predictive performance than any single constituent model could achieve alone. * **Improved Accuracy:** Ensembling typically leads to higher predictive accuracy compared to individual models, especially when the base models are diverse and reasonably accurate. * **Reduced Overfitting:** Ensembling techniques like bagging and boosting can help to reduce overfitting by averaging or weighting the predictions of multiple models. Ensembling is a powerful and versatile technique that can significantly improve the performance of machine learning models.
